text:
Vasily Podkolzin has had the kind of first quarter that changes how people talk about a player. He's playing 17:30 a night, up from 15:23 last season, he's on the ice for 37% of Edmonton's power-play chances (12% a year ago), and he has 15 points in 20 games. Our breakout flag likes it because his own chances rose too, to 1.13 expected goals per 60 minutes from 0.78.

Now the honest part. Nine goals on 6.6 expected is a 22.5% shooting rate, well above what our numbers think he is (about 14%). The last ten games have already cooled: three points, ice time down more than three minutes. One of those nights lasted 2:36, when he fought Anaheim's Drew Helleson after a hit on Connor McDavid and was thrown out, a moment that won him a lot of goodwill across Canada going by the headlines.

The process holds up. Edmonton takes 61% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there. The goal rate is what comes down.
headline: Podkolzin found his role, now the goals slow
